item.title: Archbishop Francis Duffy appointed Bishop of Killala
item.description: Archbishop of Tuam Francis Duffy has been appointed as the Bishop of Killala. The Cavan native has been holding the position of Apostolic Administrator of Killala for almost two years before his recent appointment. The decision results in the Diocese of Killala and the Archdiocese of Tuam being united under the same Bishop. Advertisement It paves the way for the formal amalgamation of the two dioceses. Bishop of Achonry and Elphin, Kevin Doran, welcomes the appointment: Advertisement

item.description: Most of action last weekend was in the Joes Bar Challenge Cup with a few shock results. Cup holders St. Johns Athletic were beaten 4–0 at Lecarrow by Mooe United. item.title: Meeting sought over Leitrim's LIS status
item.description: A meeting has been sought with Minister Dara Calleary over Co Leitrim's allocation to the Local and Community Improvement Schemes. Only 19 roads in the county were addressed under the LIS scheme in 2025. The scheme involves the state and homeowners jointly paying for the upgrade of small roads and laneways. item.title: Mass to mark anniversary of Ukrainian war
item.description: A special Mass is taking place in Longford town this evening to mark the fourth anniversary of the Ukraine war. The Mass for Peace and Justice in Ukraine is taking place in St Mel's Cathedral at 7.30pm. Russia invaded Ukraine on February 24, 2022 - with as many as 140,000 Ukrainians losing their lives since then. Advertisement Ukrainian refugees are living in 405 family homes in Co Longford. item.title: Local authority making rezoning progress
item.description: Roscommon County Council is making arrangements to start rezoning significantly more land for houses. Like all local authorities, they were ordered to do so by the government last July. But only two councils have completed the process - Mayo and Waterford - which Housing Minister James Browne says is a concern. item.title: Rally to show support for Aldi in Boyle to take place this weekend
item.description: A rally to show to support for the proposed Aldi store in Boyle is set to take place this weekend. Roscommon County Council gave the supermarket giant planning permission for the new store last month. But the decision has been appealed to An Coimisiún Pleanála, who will take four months to look into it. An event in support of the development is set to take place at the Crescent this Saturday at 2pm. Former Mayor of Boyle, Jane Suffin, is one of the organisers: Advertisement

item.description: Contracts have been signed for two major developments in county Roscommon. The first at Ballaghaderreen town park will see a 500 thousand euro development at the plots. item.title: Roscommon ladies fume over Down game venue
item.description: Roscommon boss Finbar Egan was left unimpressed after his sides meeting with Down was moved to Belfast. Down scored a 1-12 to 2-6 victory over Roscommon on Sunday afternoon. However, most annoying to Egan was the late change of venue. The game was due to take place in Pairc Esler. However, the game was moved to Belfast on Saturday evening. item.title: Emma Biesty
item.description: Emma Biesty The Walk Road, Roscommon Town. Sunday, February 22nd, peacefully in her 15th year, surrounded by her heartbroken family. In the loving and devoted care of C.H.I. Crumlin. Emma Biesty, adored daughter to Tara (née O’Callaghan) and Joe and cherished sister to Mark and Amy. She will be forever missed by her family, grandmothers; Stephanie and Maureen, uncles, aunts, cousins and her many friends. She is now reunited with her beloved grandads; Michael O’Callaghan and Joe Biesty. Reposing
